welcome.tagline: Let's get your robot vacuum a new life
welcome.find_help:
If you encounter any issues during installation, don't hesitate to get in touch on GitHub, Discord or ask your closest technical friend!

Missing a language? You can help! (see GitHub)
disclaimer.title: ~ The disclaimer ~
disclaimer.acknowledge: I will not disconnect the USB cable before instructed to do so
disclaimer.warning: I have downloaded Vacuula from github.com/vacuula, as other sources could contain nefarious modifications
disclaimer.bullet2: If your robot is rainbowing, get in touch!
disclaimer.bullet3: You will need a USB data cable
disclaimer.bullet4: Vacuula is not affiliated with Neato
disclaimer.bullet5: Vacuula modifies your robot software. It does so for the sole reason of allowing your Vacuula server to control it. All code; installer, server and scripts are open source, take a look!
disclaimer.bullet6: Make sure your robot is fully charged and connected to the charger!
disclaimer.bullet7: If you have previously done an ESP32 mod you have to remove the device prior to installing Vacuula
disclaimer.bullet8: You proceed at your own risk
serversearch.title: Vacuula needs a server
serversearch.body: Before biting your robot a server needs to be set up. Follow instructions here if not done already
serversearch.detailinfo: 🛈 The server needs to be accessible on both the network the robot will be connected to and on the network controlling devices will be - if separate

wifi.explanation: Vacuula needs to reach your server!

wifi.disclaimer: 🛈 Note that the Neato devices supported by Vacuula do not support WPA3, make sure your network uses WPA2 or WPA2/WPA3 mixed mode. The robots also only support 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi

wifi.gen23.pre.disclaimer: Just like with the original app, your robot needs to be set up via its own Wi-Fi connection. A network with the above name should show up soon! If it does not appear within a couple minutes, try restarting your computer's Wi-Fi, then the installer and lastly the robot
wifi.gen23.disclaimer: 🛈 Only networks visible to the robot can be selected. The Neato devices supported by Vacuula do not support WPA3, make sure your network uses WPA2 or WPA2/WPA3 mixed mode. The robots also only support 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi
firmware.scan: Checking if your robot's firmware is up-to-date
firmware.title: Firmware update
firmware.flair: Your robot is feeling a bit out of the loop
firmware.subtitle: Vacuula only supports the latest versions of the Neato firmware. Here we will help you update to a supported version!
firmware.install.step.awaiting_ack: Waiting for robot to acknowledge received firmware
firmware.install.step.done.gen3: Uploaded to robot! If everything went well the robot should restart by itself within 30 seconds and you will be automatically presented with the next step.
firmware.install.step.done.gen4: Uploaded to robot! It will continue flashing yellow during its update procedure which may take up to 15-20 minutes. Keep the robot connected to your computer and let it finish, we recommend some tea or coffee!
firmware.install.done.disconnected.gen3: Robot disconnected after firmware update which most likely means the update was successful
Please wait for the robot to start up; the red error light will start flashing (as the dustbin is not in place) which is expected and can be ignored. You will have to start over with some steps to continue the installation of Vacuula
firmware.install.done.disconnected.gen4: Robot disconnected after firmware update which most likely means the update was successful
Please wait for the robot to start up, typically indicated by a sound. Once that happens you will have to start over with some steps to continue the installation of Vacuula
firmware.gen3.factory_reset_ack: For the firmware update to be a guaranteed success, your robot needs to be factory reset. Please confirm that you have done so recently, or see below instructions.
firmware.gen3.factory_reset.explanation: Factory reset your Neato to guarantee a successful update. Do not disconnect the robot from the computer and follow these steps:
firmware.gen3.factory_reset.instructions:
(blue dot shows power button)

1. Remove dustbin, this should already be the case
2. Press in the two bumper switches as the red arrows show
3. Hold down power button until robot turns off, 10s
4. Release ONLY the power button when lights are off
5. Press power button once (while still holding the bumper switches)
6. Only release bumper when blue light stops flashing
firmware.gen3.factory_reset.disconnected: You are making progress! Robot disconnected, continue holding bumper switches and press power button once!

When you have pressed the power button the robot will start flashing with a blue light, you may release the bumper when the blue light stops. When the robot is fully started (red error will flash because of no dustbin), click below to restart the installer and flash the latest firmware!
firmware.gen3.factory_reset.restart: Once started, click here to restart installer and install latest firmware
